extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, trade mark practitioners, registrars, and IP law students
extracted.subtask_description: Explanatory commentary on the rules and standards under the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act 1883 governing registration, renewal, removal, assignment, inspection, evidence, and remedies for patents, designs and trade marks (including Sheffield marks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal liability for applying false or counterfeit trade marks
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who applies a false or counterfeit trade mark, or to which any false or counterfeit trade mark has been applied, or who incloses/places/attaches any chattel or article with the trade mark of any other person, or who causes/procures or aids/abets/counsels any of those offences, commits a misdemeanor and is liable to forfeiture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections cited (sects. 2,3,13). Forfeiture provisions follow; instruments used for applying marks are forfeitable. The text enumerates specific acts constituting the offence (applying, causing, aiding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture of chattels and instruments used in counterfeiting
rubrics_metrics.description: All chattels and articles to which any counterfeit trade mark is applied, every instrument for applying such a trade mark in a person's possession or power, and chattels/articles made to be used in like manner, are forfeited to Her Majesty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register entries and forfeiture are treated together. The Register of Trade Marks and prescribed rules identify what is forfeited; cross-reference to Trade Marks Rules for particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: False pretences where fraudulent imitation induces purchase
rubrics_metrics.description: Where by a fraudulent imitation of a trade mark a person induces others to buy and pay for articles in the belief they are buying certain things when they are not, that person may be convicted of obtaining money on false pretences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offence is committed even if the false representation is only as to quality or weight (cases: R. v. Ardletl; R. v. Sherwood). This is an alternative criminal remedy apart from the Trade Marks Act provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of Trade Marks must be kept at Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be kept at the Patent Office a book called the Register of Trade Marks wherein shall be entered the names and addresses of proprietors of registered trade marks, notifications of assignments and transmissions of trade marks, and such other matters as may be prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to Trade Marks Rules for prescribed matters (rules 30,44). The register is the central public record and basis for many statutory rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of proprietor's name and address on registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The name and address of the proprietor will be entered on the register on the registration of the mark; application for alteration of address may be made in Form M and is subject to a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade Marks Rules, Form M; fees specified (see Trade Marks Rules, rule 30). Practical requirement for keeping register accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to register assignment or transmission of a trade mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person becomes entitled to a trade mark by assignment, transmission, or operation of law, he may apply to be registered as proprietor by sending a request in Form K, stating particulars of the assignment/transmission sufficient to show the manner of vesting, verified by statutory declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade Marks Rules (34–39). Fees payable (first schedule). Particulars required differ in cases of death, bankruptcy etc.; see notes to sect. 55. Registration of assignments affects standing to sue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof and fees required for assignments and transmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to register assignments must be verified by statutory declaration and accompanied by prescribed fees: 1s. for first mark and 2s. for each additional mark transmitted at same time (per First Schedule to Trade Marks Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particulars required in special cases (death, bankruptcy) referenced. Failure to register may affect ability to bring infringement actions (discussion: registration appears required to maintain an action except for old marks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of original registration (fourteen years)
rubrics_metrics.description: The original registration is good for fourteen years (the text notes fourteen years and three months in practice), after which, unless a renewal fee has been paid, the mark may be removed from the register and the proprietor will be deprived of statutory rights under secs.75–77.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 79 sets timing; notices are to be sent by the comptroller. Sub-section (5) creates a special proviso preserving certain de facto effects for five years after removal for application purposes (see sect.72 reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal notice and timeline before removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Comptroller shall send notice to the registered proprietor not less than two months nor more than three months before the expiration of fourteen years that the trade mark will be removed unless the proprietor pays the prescribed renewal fee before expiration; if unpaid, a second notice is sent one month after the first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fee not paid before expiration, comptroller may after three months remove mark from register; the statutory notice regime and timelines are mandatory in form and effect (Trade Marks Rules, 30–33).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period and additional fee to prevent removal
rubrics_metrics.description: If, before the expiration of the three months after expiry, the registered proprietor pays the renewal fee together with the additional prescribed fee, the comptroller may, without removing the trade mark from the register, accept the fee as if paid before expiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional fee amount specified in rules (see First Schedule). This preserves continuity of registration if proprietor acts within the three‑month grace period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of removed marks at comptroller's discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a trade mark has been removed from the register for non-payment of the prescribed fee, the comptroller may, if satisfied that it is just to do so, restore the mark to the register on payment of the prescribed additional fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No statutory time limit for application to restore is stated; lapse of time is a factor in determining whether restoration is 'just'. Total fee example given (21s. 10d. equivalent in text). See Trade Marks Rules, 45 for record of removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removed mark deemed registered for five years for application purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade mark removed from the register for non-payment or otherwise shall nevertheless, for the purpose of any application for registration during the five years next after the date of such removal, be deemed to be a trade mark which is already registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proviso is specially related to sect.72 and prevents registration of a similar mark for the same class of goods during the five‑year period; practical effect on oppositions and new applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for applications, registrations and other matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees in respect of applications, registrations, and other matters under this part of the Act shall be those prescribed by the Board of Trade with Treasury sanction and shall be levied and paid to the Exchequer in the manner directed by the Treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First Schedule to Trade Marks Rules contains the list of prescribed fees; practical importance for calculating cost of filings, restorations, appeals, and certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheffield register restricted scope and who may obtain marks
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sheffield register (maintained by the Cutlers' Company) is restricted to marks assigned or registered by that Company in respect of raw steel, cutlery, edge-tools, goods made of steel or steel and iron combined, and to persons carrying on business in Hallamshire or within six miles thereof. Persons entitled include apprentices after seven years, parish apprentices proving service, persons carrying on certain specified trades within limits, and manufacturers of steel and edge-tools within prescribed limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical and territorial limitations; sub-sections (1)–(3) set scope. The Sheffield register replaces the old Cutlers' register and marks not transferred within five years are deemed abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedure for Sheffield marks (form, duplicate, fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for registration of a trade mark used on specified goods by persons carrying on business in Hallamshire (or within six miles) are to be made to the Cutlers' Company, in duplicate (Form F), governed by the general provisions and rules of the Act, and fees payable are the same as for other marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every application must be notified to the comptroller who may stop acceptance subject to appeal (sub-sects. (3)–(5)); Trade Marks Rules, 53 prescribes duplicate requirement and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to comptroller and objection timeframe for Sheffield applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cutlers' Company shall notify the comptroller within seven days after receipt of an application by sending a copy of the application and two representations of the mark for each class; the comptroller must give notice of objection, if any, within one month of receipt of the notice from the Company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the comptroller objects, the Cutlers' Company must not proceed and any aggrieved person may appeal to the Court; appeal to comptroller also available. Trade Marks Rules, 54 govern procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date and effect of registration in Sheffield register
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon registration of a trade mark in the Sheffield register the Cutlers' Company shall give notice to the comptroller who shall enter the mark in the register of trade marks; such registration shall bear date as of the day of application to the Cutlers' Company and have the same effect as if the application had been made to the comptroller on that day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables the comptroller to keep central records and ensures continuity of rights and expiry/renewal computation as if applied to the central register on that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application by persons outside Hallamshire must be notified to Cutlers' Company
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the comptroller receives an application from a person not carrying on business in Hallamshire for registration of a trade mark used on specified goods, he shall notify the application and proceedings thereon to the Cutlers' Company by sending the Official Journal copy with a distinguishing note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects the Cutlers' Company's local register rights and enables them to object where applicable (Trade Marks Rules, 54(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closing of Cutlers' register and abandonment if not transferred
rubrics_metrics.description: At the expiration of five years from commencement of the Act the Cutlers' register shall be closed and all marks entered therein shall, unless entered in the Sheffield register, be deemed to have been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five-year transition period intended for transfer of marks from old to new register; practical consequence for proprietors who fail to transfer marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of bodies and multiple marks in Sheffield register
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may be registered as proprietor of two or more trade marks and a body (corporate or unincorporate) may be registered as proprietor of a trade mark or trade marks in the Sheffield register notwithstanding earlier Cutlers' Company statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits multiple registrations and corporate proprietorship despite prior constraints in older local Acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedures from Cutlers' Company decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Cutlers' Company may appeal to the comptroller in the prescribed manner; the comptroller can confirm, reverse or modify the decision, subject to further appeal to the Court. Fee for appeal to the comptroller is 1s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form of appeal to comptroller is in Trade Marks Forms (Form W); further appeal procedures are in Trade Marks Rules, rule 29. Administrative and judicial review path is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Cutlers' Company's summary punishment provisions to Sheffield marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of the Cutlers' Company's Acts relating to the summary punishment of persons counterfeiting Sheffield corporate marks (e.g., the fifth section of the Company's Act of 1814) apply to any mark entered in the Sheffield register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves local summary remedies for counterfeiting alongside statutory remedies under the Act; see Appendix C references for historical Acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office establishment and comptroller-general role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treasury may provide an office called the Patent Office; until then existing Commissioners' offices serve as Patent Office. The Patent Office shall be under control of the comptroller-general of patents, designs, and trade marks who acts under Board of Trade superintendence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board of Trade appoints the comptroller-general, examiners, officers and clerks subject to Treasury approval; salaries and expenses paid by Parliament. Practical rubric for administration and delegation (acts may be done by authorised officers in comptroller's absence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Seal of the Patent Office and evidential notice
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be a seal for the Patent Office and impressions thereof shall be judicially noticed and admitted in evidence; copies of documents sealed with the seal and certified by the comptroller are receivable in evidence without proof or production of originals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 84–89 detail that certified sealed copies/extracts are admissible in all Courts in Her Majesty's dominions; for designs and trade marks the legal proceeding for which certificate is granted must be stated (Designs Rules 57; Trade Marks Rules 34). Fees for certifying provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: No entry of trusts on registers
rubrics_metrics.description: No notice of any trust, expressed, implied, or constructive, shall be entered in any register under the Act or be receivable by the comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registers record legal title and proprietary entries only; equitable interests (trusts) are not entered and must be enforced by ordinary equitable remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registers kept under the Act (list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registers kept under the Act include: the register of patents (sect.23), the register of designs (sect.55), the register of trade marks (sect.78), and the Sheffield register of trade marks (sect.81).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each register has its own rules for inspection, copies, assignments, and remedies; cross-reference to respective sections and rules is required for procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal ground: contrary to law or morality
rubrics_metrics.description: The comptroller may refuse to grant a patent or to register a design or trade mark if, in his opinion, the use would be contrary to law or morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters patent historically contained a clause voiding grants contrary to law or prejudicial to subjects in general; administrative discretion exists to refuse on public policy/morality grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of assignments/transmissions into registers on proof to comptroller
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person becomes entitled by assignment, transmission, or operation of law to a patent, copyright in a registered design, or a registered trade mark, the comptroller shall, on request and after proof of title to his satisfaction, cause the name of such person to be entered as proprietor in the relevant register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms of request indicated in Patents/Designs/Trade Marks Forms; effect of entry is that the registered proprietor has power absolutely to assign, grant licences, otherwise deal with the subject and give effectual receipts, subject to equities enforceable as in respect of other personal property. Discussion on whether unregistered assignee may sue (patents, designs, trade marks) notes registration is important to enforce rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registers open to public inspection and certified copies on payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Every register kept under the Act shall at all convenient times be open to public inspection subject to prescribed regulations; certified copies sealed with the Patent Office seal of any entry shall be given on payment of the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents Rules 75 and Trade Marks/Designs Rules provide detail; fees for office copies are per 100 words (minimums); designs copy availability differs (only when copyright expired except certificates of existence under sect.53).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealed certified copies and extracts admissible as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed or written copies or extracts certified by the comptroller and sealed with the Patent Office seal of patents, specifications, disclaimers and other documents in the Patent Office, and of registers/books kept there, shall be admitted in evidence in all Courts and proceedings without further proof or production of originals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate for designs/trade marks must state legal proceeding for which certificate granted (Designs Rules 57; Trade Marks Rules 34). Copies are deposited in named repositories for Scotland, Ireland, Isle of Man (sect.100) and admissible there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of registers by the Court
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may, on application of any person aggrieved by omission without sufficient cause of a name from any register or by any entry made without sufficient cause, make orders for making, expunging, or varying the entry as it thinks fit, may decide necessary questions, direct issues to be tried, award damages, and order that due notice of rectification be given to the comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rectification jurisdiction extends to all registers under the Act (extends principle of Trade Marks Registration Act 1875); costs and consequential directions are at the Court's discretion; remedy for aggrieved parties.
